restatement.stem: Had the warning been issued earlier, many residents could have left the area in time.

restatement.stem: Not only did the new policy reduce costs, but it also improved employee satisfaction.

restatement.stem: It was not until the late nineteenth century that the cause of malaria was discovered.

restatement.explanation: Only after... did = רק אחרי... = not... until. החוקרים הבחינו בטעות רק בבדיקה השנייה. אפשרות 4 הופכת את סדר האירועים, ואפשרות 3 מדברת על מתי הטעות קרתה ולא מתי התגלתה.

restatement.stem: Regardless of the weather, the ceremony will take place outdoors.
options: The ceremony will be held outside whatever the weather is like.
If the weather is bad, the ceremony will be moved indoors.
The ceremony will take place outdoors only if the weather is good.
The weather will decide whether the ceremony is held outdoors.
restatement.explanation: Regardless of = without considering (בלי קשר ל-). הטקס יתקיים בחוץ בכל מזג אוויר. כל שאר האפשרויות הופכות את מזג האוויר לתנאי — ההפך מהמשפט המקורי.

restatement.stem: The new library is twice as large as the old one.
options: The new library has two floors, unlike the old one.
The old library was half the size of the new one.
The old library was twice as large as the new one.
The new library is slightly larger than the old one.
restatement.explanation: twice as large = גדולה פי שניים. אם החדשה גדולה פי שניים, הישנה היא בחצי מגודלה. היזהרו מתשובה שהופכת את הכיוון.

restatement.stem: She regrets not having accepted the job offer.
options: She is glad that she did not accept the job offer.
She regrets accepting the job offer.
She is sorry that she turned down the job offer.
She has not yet decided whether to accept the job offer.
restatement.explanation: היא מצטערת שלא קיבלה את ההצעה = היא מצטערת שדחתה אותה (turned down). שימו לב ל-not: התשובה השנייה הפוכה.

restatement.stem: The storm caused far less damage than had been expected.
options: The storm caused more damage than anyone had predicted.
Nobody expected the storm to cause any damage.
The damage from the storm was exactly as expected.
The damage caused by the storm was much smaller than predicted.
restatement.explanation: far less than expected = הרבה פחות מהצפוי. far מחזק את ההשוואה.

restatement.stem: Under no circumstances should the door be left unlocked.
options: The door must always be locked.
In some circumstances, the door may be left unlocked.
The door should never be locked.
The door is usually left unlocked.
restatement.explanation: Under no circumstances = בשום מקרה (היפוך תחבירי עם should). אסור אף פעם להשאיר את הדלת לא נעולה — כלומר היא חייבת להיות נעולה תמיד. שימו לב לשלילה הכפולה (no + unlocked).

restatement.stem: Neither the manager nor her assistant was aware of the problem.
options: Only the manager knew about the problem.
Both the manager and her assistant were unaware of the problem.
The assistant told the manager about the problem.
Either the manager or her assistant was aware of the problem.
restatement.explanation: Neither... nor = לא זה ולא זה. אף אחד מהשניים לא ידע על הבעיה.

restatement.stem: As far as the researchers know, no one has ever crossed the desert on foot.
options: The researchers have crossed the desert on foot.
Many people have crossed the desert, but not on foot.
According to the researchers' knowledge, the desert has never been crossed on foot.
The researchers know that the desert is too far to cross on foot.
restatement.explanation: As far as ... know = למיטב ידיעתם. המשפט אינו קובע עובדה מוחלטת אלא את מה שהחוקרים יודעים. התשובה האחרונה מנצלת את המילה far בצורה מטעה.

restatement.stem: The company would have gone bankrupt if it had not received a government loan.
options: The company went bankrupt despite the government loan.
The company did not need a government loan.
The company went bankrupt because the government refused to lend it money.
The government loan saved the company from bankruptcy.
restatement.explanation: תנאי מסוג שלישי (would have... if... had not) מתאר מצב שלא קרה: החברה קיבלה הלוואה ולכן לא פשטה רגל. ההלוואה הצילה אותה.

restatement.stem: The play was so popular that tickets sold out within hours.
options: Because so many people wanted to see the play, all the tickets were sold very quickly.
The play was not popular, so tickets were cheap.
Tickets for the play were available for several weeks.
The play became popular only after the tickets were sold.
restatement.explanation: so... that מבטא סיבה ותוצאה: ההצגה הייתה כה פופולרית שהכרטיסים אזלו תוך שעות.

restatement.stem: In terms of population, Tel Aviv is smaller than Jerusalem.
options: Tel Aviv has more residents than Jerusalem.
Jerusalem has more residents than Tel Aviv.
Tel Aviv covers a smaller area than Jerusalem.
Jerusalem and Tel Aviv have similar populations.
restatement.explanation: In terms of population = מבחינת אוכלוסייה. בירושלים יש יותר תושבים. התשובה השלישית מדברת על שטח ולא על אוכלוסייה.

restatement.stem: The professor insisted that every student submit the assignment on time.
options: The professor allowed some students to submit the assignment late.
Every student asked the professor for more time.
The professor demanded that all students hand in the assignment by the deadline.
The professor submitted the assignment on time.
restatement.explanation: insisted that = עמד על כך / דרש. submit = hand in (להגיש). הפרופסור דרש שכולם יגישו בזמן.

restatement.stem: It is widely assumed that the ancient wall was built for defense, but there is little evidence for this.
options: There is strong evidence that the wall was built for defense.
Few people believe that the wall was built for defense.
The wall was not built for defense, as the evidence clearly shows.
Although many believe the wall was built for protection, this belief is not well supported.
restatement.explanation: widely assumed = רבים מניחים. little evidence = מעט ראיות (לא ׳אין ראיות כלל׳ ולא הוכחה הפוכה). התשובה השלישית מוגזמת — המשפט לא קובע שהחומה לא נבנתה להגנה.

restatement.stem: The longer the negotiations continued, the less likely an agreement seemed.
options: As the negotiations went on, an agreement appeared increasingly unlikely.
The negotiations were long because both sides wanted an agreement.
An agreement was reached after long negotiations.
Short negotiations rarely lead to an agreement.
restatement.explanation: The... -er, the less... = ככל ש... כך פחות. ככל שהמו״מ נמשך, הסיכוי להסכם נראה קטן יותר.

restatement.stem: Despite being the youngest member of the team, she was chosen as its leader.
options: She was chosen as leader because she was the youngest member.
She was selected to lead the team even though she was younger than all the others.
The youngest member of the team refused to lead it.
She was the oldest member, but she was not chosen as leader.
restatement.explanation: Despite = למרות. היא נבחרה למרות גילה הצעיר, לא בגללו (התשובה הראשונה הופכת ניגוד לסיבה).

restatement.stem: Scarcely had the guests arrived when the lights went out.
options: The guests arrived after the lights had gone out.
Very few guests arrived before the lights went out.
The lights went out almost immediately after the guests arrived.
The lights went out, so the guests did not arrive.
restatement.explanation: Scarcely had... when = אך ורק... ומיד. האורחים בקושי הגיעו והחשמל כבר כבה. scarcely כאן מתייחס לזמן, לא לכמות האורחים.

restatement.stem: The museum is open to the public every day except Mondays.
options: The museum is open only on Mondays.
The museum is closed to the public every day.
On Mondays, the museum is open only to members of the public.
The public can visit the museum on any day but Monday.
restatement.explanation: except = but (חוץ מ-). המוזיאון פתוח בכל יום חוץ מיום שני.

restatement.stem: The findings cast doubt on the widely held view that the disease is inherited.
options: The results raise questions about the common belief that the disease is passed down in families.
The results confirm that the disease is inherited.
Few people believe that the disease is inherited.
The findings show that the disease cannot be cured.
restatement.explanation: cast doubt on = מעורר ספק לגבי. widely held view = דעה רווחת. inherited = עובר בתורשה (passed down in families).

restatement.stem: Not a single error was found in the report.
options: Only one error was found in the report.
The report was completely free of mistakes.
The report contained a few errors.
Nobody looked for errors in the report.
restatement.explanation: Not a single = אף לא אחת. לא נמצאה אפילו טעות אחת. היזהרו מ-single שמטעה לכיוון ׳טעות אחת׳.

restatement.stem: He could not have stolen the money, since he was abroad at the time.
options: He stole the money and then went abroad.
He was unable to steal the money because it was kept abroad.
It is impossible that he took the money, because he was in another country when it disappeared.
He might have stolen the money before going abroad.
restatement.explanation: could not have + V3 = לא ייתכן ש... (מסקנה לוגית על העבר). since כאן = because: הוא היה בחו״ל.

restatement.stem: Most of the town's residents are opposed to the construction of the new airport.
options: Few of the town's residents object to the new airport.
The new airport was built despite the residents' support.
All the town's residents support the new airport.
The majority of the people living in the town are against building the airport.
restatement.explanation: Most = the majority (רוב). opposed to = against (מתנגדים ל-).

restatement.stem: The bridge, which was completed in 1932, is still in use today.
options: The bridge has been used since it was finished in 1932.
The bridge was used until 1932.
Construction of the bridge began in 1932 and has not yet ended.
The bridge was rebuilt in 1932 and closed soon after.
restatement.explanation: completed = הושלם. still in use = עדיין בשימוש. הגשר משמש מאז 1932 ועד היום.

restatement.stem: Were the government to raise taxes, many small businesses would close.
options: Because the government raised taxes, many small businesses closed.
If the government increased taxes, many small businesses would shut down.
Many small businesses closed, so the government raised taxes.
The government will not raise taxes, so small businesses will not close.
restatement.explanation: Were... to = If... (תנאי בהיפוך תחבירי). המשפט מתאר מצב היפותטי: אם הממשלה תעלה מסים — עסקים ייסגרו. זה לא קרה בפועל.

restatement.stem: She is said to be the best surgeon in the country.
options: She says that she is the best surgeon in the country.
It has been proven that she is the best surgeon in the country.
People say that she is the finest surgeon in the country.
She was told that she was the best surgeon in the country.
restatement.explanation: is said to be = אומרים עליה ש... (סביל). לא היא אומרת, וזו אינה עובדה מוכחת.

restatement.stem: The prize was awarded to the youngest of the three finalists.
options: The youngest finalist awarded the prize.
All three finalists received prizes.
The prize went to the oldest finalist.
Of the three finalists, the one who was the youngest received the prize.
restatement.explanation: was awarded to = הוענק ל-. הצעיר מבין שלושת המועמדים בגמר קיבל את הפרס. התשובה הראשונה הופכת את הסביל לפעיל.

restatement.stem: There is no point in arguing with him; he never changes his mind.
options: Arguing with him is useless, because he always sticks to his opinion.
He enjoys arguing, but he never changes his mind.
He often changes his mind after an argument.
It is important to argue with him so that he changes his mind.
restatement.explanation: There is no point in = אין טעם ב-. אין טעם להתווכח איתו כי הוא אף פעם לא משנה את דעתו.

restatement.stem: The experiment was repeated several times in order to rule out the possibility of error.
options: The experiment was repeated because an error had been found.
The experiment was carried out more than once to make sure the results were not caused by a mistake.
Several errors were found when the experiment was repeated.
The experiment was performed only once, so errors were possible.
restatement.explanation: rule out = לשלול. in order to = כדי. הניסוי חזר על עצמו כדי לשלול טעות — לא כי נמצאה טעות.

restatement.stem: It took the workers three years to restore the old church.
options: The old church was built in three years.
The workers restored the church three years ago.
The restoration of the old church lasted three years.
The old church was restored three times.
restatement.explanation: It took... three years = נדרשו שלוש שנים. restore = לשחזר/לשפץ (לא לבנות).

restatement.stem: But for her quick thinking, the accident would have been much worse.
options: Her quick thinking caused the accident.
Even though she thought quickly, the accident was very serious.
The accident happened because she did not think quickly enough.
Her fast reaction prevented the accident from being far more serious.
restatement.explanation: But for = If it had not been for (אלמלא). אלמלא חשבה מהר, התאונה הייתה חמורה בהרבה — כלומר המחשבה המהירה מנעה החמרה.

restatement.stem: The ancient Egyptians are believed to have used this tool for measuring land.
options: It is thought that the ancient Egyptians measured land with this tool.
The ancient Egyptians believed that the tool could measure land.
It has been proven that the tool was used by the Egyptians.
The tool was used to measure the land of ancient Egypt in modern times.
restatement.explanation: are believed to have used = מאמינים (חוקרים) שהם השתמשו. זו הערכה, לא הוכחה, ולא המצרים הם שהאמינו.

restatement.stem: The company's profits have doubled since the new director took over.
options: The new director doubled his own salary.
Since the arrival of the new director, the company has earned twice as much.
The company's profits fell after the new director took over.
The company has had two directors since its profits rose.
restatement.explanation: doubled = הוכפלו. took over = נכנס לתפקיד. מאז כניסת המנהל החדש הרווחים גדלו פי שניים.

restatement.stem: Whatever the outcome of the trial, the case has already damaged his reputation.
options: His reputation will be damaged only if he loses the trial.
If he wins the trial, his reputation will be restored.
No matter how the trial ends, his reputation has already been harmed.
The trial has not yet affected his reputation.
restatement.explanation: Whatever the outcome = No matter how it ends (לא משנה מה תהיה התוצאה). הנזק לשמו כבר נגרם.

restatement.stem: The novel is less a love story than a study of social class.
options: The novel is mainly a love story.
The novel is neither a love story nor a study of social class.
Love stories are less popular than novels about social class.
The novel deals more with social class than with romance.
restatement.explanation: less X than Y = פחות X ויותר Y. הרומן הוא בעיקר עיון במעמדות חברתיים ופחות סיפור אהבה.

restatement.stem: The meeting has been brought forward from Thursday to Tuesday.
options: The meeting will now take place earlier, on Tuesday instead of Thursday.
The meeting has been moved from Tuesday to Thursday.
The meeting will take place on both Tuesday and Thursday.
The meeting was cancelled on Tuesday.
restatement.explanation: bring forward = להקדים. הפגישה הוקדמה מחמישי לשלישי.

restatement.stem: Visitors are requested to refrain from taking photographs inside the building.
options: Visitors are encouraged to take photographs inside the building.
Visitors are asked not to take pictures inside the building.
Visitors may take photographs only inside the building.
Photographs of visitors are taken inside the building.
restatement.explanation: refrain from = להימנע מ-. are requested = מתבקשים. המבקרים מתבקשים לא לצלם בתוך הבניין.

restatement.stem: It was the lack of funding, rather than a lack of interest, that ended the project.
options: The project ended because nobody was interested in it.
The project had both enough funding and enough interest.
The project ended because there was not enough money, not because people were uninterested.
Interest in the project grew after its funding ended.
restatement.explanation: It was X, rather than Y, that... = X (ולא Y) הוא שגרם. הסיבה לסיום הייתה מחסור בכסף, לא חוסר עניין.

restatement.stem: Only a handful of the original buildings survived the fire.
options: Most of the original buildings survived the fire.
None of the original buildings survived the fire.
The fire started in a handful of the original buildings.
Very few of the original buildings were left standing after the fire.
restatement.explanation: a handful = קומץ, מספר קטן. רק מעט מהבניינים המקוריים שרדו — לא אף אחד ולא רובם.

restatement.stem: He is not so much lazy as unmotivated.
options: His problem is a lack of motivation rather than laziness.
He is both lazy and unmotivated.
He is lazy but highly motivated.
He is more lazy than he is unmotivated.
restatement.explanation: not so much X as Y = לא כל כך X אלא יותר Y. הבעיה שלו היא חוסר מוטיבציה, לא עצלות.

restatement.stem: The disease, once common throughout Europe, is now extremely rare.
options: The disease has always been rare in Europe.
The disease used to be widespread in Europe, but today it is very uncommon.
The disease is becoming more common in Europe.
The disease was rare in Europe but is now common.
restatement.explanation: once common = הייתה נפוצה בעבר. now extremely rare = כיום נדירה מאוד.

restatement.stem: She would rather walk to work than take the crowded bus.
options: She has to walk because the bus is always full.
She takes the bus because she dislikes walking.
She prefers walking to work over riding the crowded bus.
She walks to work only when the bus is crowded.
restatement.explanation: would rather X than Y = מעדיפה X על פני Y. זו העדפה, לא חובה (has to).

restatement.stem: The report makes no mention of the costs involved.
options: The report focuses mainly on costs.
The report mentions only some of the costs.
The costs of the report were not mentioned.
The report says nothing about how much it will cost.
restatement.explanation: makes no mention of = לא מזכיר כלל. הדו״ח לא אומר דבר על העלויות. התשובה השלישית מדברת על עלות הדו״ח עצמו.

restatement.stem: So successful was the campaign that it was copied by organizations around the world.
options: The campaign was so effective that organizations worldwide imitated it.
The campaign succeeded because it copied other organizations.
Organizations around the world tried to stop the campaign.
The campaign was copied, but it was not successful.
restatement.explanation: So + adj + was... that = היפוך של The campaign was so successful that. ההצלחה גרמה לארגונים בעולם לחקות את הקמפיין.

readingComprehension.title: The Return of the Wolves
paragraphs: In 1995, after an absence of nearly seventy years, gray wolves were reintroduced into Yellowstone National Park in the United States. Wolves had been deliberately eliminated from the park in the early twentieth century, when they were viewed mainly as a threat to livestock and to popular game animals such as elk.

Without their main predator, elk populations grew rapidly. Large herds spent long periods grazing along riverbanks, where they consumed young willow and aspen trees before the trees could mature. As these trees declined, riverbanks became less stable, and animals that depended on them, such as beavers and many songbirds, became increasingly rare.

The return of the wolves appeared to reverse this process. Elk numbers fell, and, perhaps more importantly, the remaining elk began to avoid open areas near rivers, where they could easily be hunted. In several locations, willows recovered and beaver colonies returned. Ecologists describe such a chain of effects, in which a predator indirectly influences plants and other species, as a "trophic cascade."

Not all researchers, however, accept this dramatic account. Some point out that a series of dry years, an increase in the number of bears, and human hunting outside the park also reduced the elk population during the same period. In their view, the wolves played a role, but the recovery of Yellowstone cannot be explained by a single factor.

questions.stem: According to the second paragraph, the decline of willow and aspen trees was caused by -
options: a series of unusually dry years
elk feeding along the rivers
beavers cutting down young trees
the return of the wolves
questions.explanation: בפסקה 2 נכתב שעדרי האיילים רעו לאורך הגדות ואכלו את העצים הצעירים לפני שהספיקו לגדול. השנים היבשות מוזכרות רק בפסקה 4 ובהקשר אחר.

questions.stem: The term "trophic cascade" (paragraph 3) refers to -
options: the sudden disappearance of a predator from an ecosystem
the movement of animals away from rivers
a series of indirect effects that a predator has on an ecosystem
the method ecologists use to count elk
questions.explanation: המונח מוגדר בפסקה עצמה: a chain of effects, in which a predator indirectly influences plants and other species — שרשרת של השפעות עקיפות של טורף על המערכת האקולוגית.

questions.stem: The main purpose of the last paragraph is to -
options: provide further evidence that the wolves saved Yellowstone
describe how bears compete with wolves for food
explain why wolves were removed from the park
suggest that the recovery had several causes, not only the wolves
questions.explanation: הפסקה פותחת ב-however ומציגה עמדה מסתייגת: גורמים נוספים (בצורת, דובים, ציד) תרמו לירידת מספר האיילים, ולכן ההתאוששות אינה נובעת מגורם יחיד.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that in the early twentieth century, wolves were -
options: considered harmful to human interests
protected by law within the park
the main food source of bears
studied closely by ecologists
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1 נכתב שהזאבים חוסלו בכוונה כי נתפסו כאיום על משק החי ועל חיות ציד — כלומר נחשבו מזיקים לאינטרסים של בני אדם.

readingComprehension.title: Why We Forget
paragraphs: In the 1880s, the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus carried out one of the first scientific studies of memory. Using himself as the only subject, he memorized long lists of meaningless syllables, such as "WID" and "ZOF," and then tested how many he could recall after different periods of time.

His results revealed a pattern now known as the "forgetting curve." Most of the forgetting took place within the first hour or so after learning; after that, the rate of forgetting slowed considerably. Ebbinghaus chose meaningless syllables deliberately: because they had no connection to anything he already knew, he could measure memory without the influence of prior knowledge.

Ebbinghaus also noticed that reviewing material several times over a few days was far more effective than studying it repeatedly in a single session. This finding, known as the "spacing effect," has since been confirmed in hundreds of experiments with learners of all ages.

Despite this evidence, many students continue to rely on last-minute "cramming" before exams. One reason may be that cramming produces a feeling of mastery: material studied an hour ago seems familiar. Unfortunately, this sense of familiarity is misleading, since much of the material is likely to be forgotten within days.

questions.stem: Ebbinghaus used meaningless syllables in order to -
options: make the experiment more enjoyable
prevent existing knowledge from affecting the results
test his ability to learn foreign languages
compare his memory with that of other subjects
questions.explanation: בפסקה 2: ההברות נבחרו כי אין להן קשר לידע קודם, וכך אפשר למדוד זיכרון without the influence of prior knowledge. התשובה "compare his memory with that of other subjects" שגויה — הוא היה הנבדק היחיד.

questions.stem: According to the "forgetting curve" (paragraph 2), -
options: forgetting occurs at a constant rate
most information is forgotten only after several weeks
forgetting is fastest shortly after learning
meaningful material is never forgotten
questions.explanation: Most of the forgetting took place within the first hour — רוב השכחה מתרחשת זמן קצר אחרי הלמידה, ואחר כך הקצב מאט. לכן הקצב אינו קבוע.

questions.stem: The word "misleading" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to -
options: giving a false impression
difficult to describe
extremely pleasant
easy to change
questions.explanation: misleading = מטעה. תחושת ההיכרות נותנת רושם כוזב של שליטה בחומר, שכן החומר יישכח תוך ימים.

questions.stem: The author would most likely advise a student preparing for an exam to -
options: study the material intensively the night before
memorize lists of meaningless syllables
avoid reviewing material that has already been studied
review the material several times over a period of days
questions.explanation: הכותב מציג את אפקט הריווח (spacing effect) כיעיל ומבקר את שיטת ה-cramming. לכן הוא היה ממליץ לחזור על החומר כמה פעמים לאורך כמה ימים.

readingComprehension.title: The Secret of Roman Concrete
paragraphs: Many structures built by the ancient Romans, such as the Pantheon in Rome and harbor walls along the Mediterranean coast, are still standing after nearly two thousand years. Modern concrete, by contrast, often begins to crack and crumble within a few decades, particularly when it is exposed to seawater.

For a long time, the secret of Roman concrete was poorly understood. Researchers knew that the Romans mixed lime with volcanic ash, but only recently have they discovered how this mixture behaves over time. When seawater seeps into Roman harbor walls, it reacts with the volcanic material and gradually forms new minerals. Instead of weakening the structure, these minerals fill tiny cracks and actually make the concrete stronger.

Another surprising feature is the presence of small white lumps of lime scattered throughout the material. Scientists once assumed that these lumps were evidence of careless mixing. However, recent studies suggest that they serve an important purpose: when water enters a crack and reaches one of the lumps, the lime dissolves and then hardens again, sealing the crack before it can spread.

Engineers are now exploring whether similar techniques could be used today. If modern concrete could repair itself in this way, buildings and bridges might last much longer, reducing both construction costs and the large amount of carbon dioxide released in the production of cement.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, modern concrete differs from Roman concrete in that it -
options: is used mainly in harbor walls
tends to deteriorate much more quickly
contains a larger amount of volcanic ash
cannot be exposed to air
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1 נכתב שבטון מודרני מתחיל להיסדק ולהתפורר תוך עשורים ספורים, בעוד מבנים רומיים עומדים כמעט אלפיים שנה. כלומר הבטון המודרני מתבלה מהר הרבה יותר.

questions.stem: What happens when seawater enters Roman harbor walls (paragraph 2)?
options: The volcanic ash dissolves and the walls weaken.
The lime separates from the volcanic ash.
New minerals form and strengthen the concrete.
Tiny cracks appear and slowly spread.
questions.explanation: לפי פסקה 2, מי הים מגיבים עם החומר הוולקני ויוצרים מינרלים חדשים, שממלאים סדקים זעירים ומחזקים את הבטון במקום להחליש אותו (Instead of weakening the structure).

questions.stem: The white lumps of lime (paragraph 3) were originally thought to be -
options: a sign that the material had been poorly mixed
a deliberate method of sealing cracks
a type of volcanic ash
the result of exposure to seawater
questions.explanation: Scientists once assumed that these lumps were evidence of careless mixing: בעבר חשבו שהגושים מעידים על ערבוב רשלני. התפקיד של איטום סדקים התגלה רק במחקרים חדשים.

questions.stem: The main purpose of the last paragraph is to -
options: describe a disadvantage of Roman building methods
explain how cement is produced
compare the cost of ancient and modern buildings
suggest a possible practical application of the findings
questions.explanation: הפסקה האחרונה עוסקת בשאלה אם אפשר ליישם את השיטה הרומית היום, ובתועלת האפשרית (מבנים עמידים יותר, פחות פחמן דו-חמצני). כלומר היא מציעה יישום מעשי של הממצאים.

readingComprehension.title: The Bilingual Advantage?
paragraphs: For much of the twentieth century, many parents and educators believed that raising a child with two languages would cause confusion and slow down the child's development. Some schools even advised immigrant families to speak only the local language at home.

From the 1960s onward, this view began to change. A number of studies reported that bilingual children performed better than monolingual children on tasks requiring attention and self-control, such as ignoring irrelevant information or switching quickly between two rules. Researchers suggested that constantly managing two languages trains the brain's general control system, much as physical exercise strengthens a muscle.

More recently, however, this so-called "bilingual advantage" has been called into question. Several large studies, involving thousands of participants, have found little or no difference between bilinguals and monolinguals on such tasks. Critics have also pointed out that studies with positive results are more likely to be published than studies that find nothing, which may have created a misleading picture.

Even so, few researchers today would return to the earlier view. Whether or not bilingualism sharpens general mental skills, there is no evidence that it harms children's development, and knowing two languages offers obvious social, cultural and professional benefits.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, some schools advised immigrant families to -
options: teach their children two languages from birth
avoid using their native language at home
send their children to bilingual schools
delay teaching their children to read
questions.explanation: Some schools even advised immigrant families to speak only the local language at home: בתי ספר המליצו לדבר בבית רק בשפה המקומית, כלומר להימנע משפת האם.

questions.stem: The comparison to "physical exercise" in paragraph 2 is used to explain -
options: how managing two languages might improve mental control
why bilingual children are physically healthier
why some children find learning languages tiring
how researchers measured attention
questions.explanation: ההשוואה לאימון גופני ממחישה את הרעיון: כמו שאימון מחזק שריר, ההתמודדות המתמדת עם שתי שפות "מאמנת" את מערכת השליטה של המוח. זו אנלוגיה, לא טענה על בריאות גופנית.

questions.stem: According to the critics mentioned in paragraph 3, the "bilingual advantage" may have seemed stronger than it really is because -
options: bilingual participants were generally older
the tasks used were too easy
studies that found no difference were less likely to be published
monolingual children refused to take part
questions.explanation: המבקרים טוענים שמחקרים עם תוצאות חיוביות מתפרסמים יותר ממחקרים שלא מצאו דבר, ולכן התמונה שהצטיירה הייתה מטעה (misleading). זוהי "הטיית פרסום".

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the author's conclusion in paragraph 4?
options: Bilingualism is harmful only if it begins in early childhood.
The bilingual advantage has finally been proven.
Schools should once again discourage the use of two languages.
Even without a mental advantage, bilingualism is beneficial and not harmful.
questions.explanation: הכותב קובע שגם אם הדו-לשוניות לא משפרת כישורים מנטליים (Whether or not...), אין עדות לנזק, ויש לה יתרונות חברתיים, תרבותיים ומקצועיים ברורים.

readingComprehension.title: Urban Heat Islands
paragraphs: On a summer afternoon, the center of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the countryside around it. This phenomenon, known as the "urban heat island" effect, was first described in the early nineteenth century by the English scientist Luke Howard, who noticed that temperatures in London were consistently higher than those in nearby villages.

Several factors contribute to the effect. Dark surfaces such as asphalt roads and roofs absorb large amounts of solar energy during the day and release it slowly at night. Cities also have far fewer trees and plants, which normally cool the air by releasing water vapor. In addition, cars, air conditioners and factories produce heat of their own.

The consequences can be serious. Higher temperatures increase the demand for air conditioning, which in turn raises energy consumption and, ironically, adds even more heat to the streets. During heat waves, the effect can also be dangerous to health, particularly for elderly people and for those who live in poorly ventilated apartments.

Fortunately, the problem can be reduced. Some cities now encourage "cool roofs," which are painted white or covered with reflective materials, while others are planting thousands of trees along their streets. Studies suggest that such measures can lower local temperatures noticeably, although they cannot eliminate the effect entirely.

questions.stem: Luke Howard is mentioned in paragraph 1 as the person who -
options: first recorded that a city was warmer than its surroundings
invented a method for cooling cities
studied the effect of heat on elderly people
measured temperatures in villages around the world
questions.explanation: לפי פסקה 1, לוק הווארד היה הראשון שתיאר את התופעה: הוא הבחין שהטמפרטורות בלונדון גבוהות באופן עקבי מאלה שבכפרים הסמוכים.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, trees and plants help to -
options: absorb solar energy during the day
cool the air around them
reduce the number of cars in cities
reflect sunlight back into the sky
questions.explanation: trees and plants ... normally cool the air by releasing water vapor: עצים וצמחים מקררים את האוויר. ספיגת אנרגיית השמש מתוארת באותה פסקה, אבל היא תכונה של משטחים כהים.

questions.stem: The word "ironically" in paragraph 3 suggests that air conditioning -
options: is too expensive for most city residents
is especially important for elderly people
contributes to the very problem it is used to solve
was not available in Luke Howard's time
questions.explanation: האירוניה היא שמזגנים, שנועדו להתמודד עם החום, מוסיפים בעצמם עוד חום לרחובות. כלומר הם מחמירים את הבעיה שהם אמורים לפתור.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from paragraph 4 that the measures described -
options: have completely solved the problem in some cities
are too expensive to be used widely
have had no measurable effect on temperatures
can help, but are only a partial solution
questions.explanation: הצעדים מורידים טמפרטורות באופן מורגש, although they cannot eliminate the effect entirely: הם עוזרים, אבל לא מעלימים את התופעה לגמרי. כלומר זהו פתרון חלקי.

readingComprehension.title: Sleep and the Teenage Brain
paragraphs: For decades, parents and teachers have complained that teenagers stay up too late and are difficult to wake in the morning. This behavior was usually explained as a matter of poor discipline or too much time spent in front of screens. Recent research, however, suggests that the explanation is largely biological.

During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts. The brain begins to release melatonin, the hormone that signals that it is time to sleep, about two hours later than it did in childhood. As a result, many teenagers simply do not feel tired until close to midnight, even if they go to bed earlier. Yet they still need between eight and ten hours of sleep each night.

Because most schools begin early in the morning, the majority of teenagers are chronically short of sleep. Studies have linked this lack of sleep to lower grades, poorer concentration, and a higher risk of car accidents among young drivers. Some researchers also see a connection between insufficient sleep and depression, although the direction of cause and effect is not yet clear.

In response to these findings, several school districts in the United States have moved their starting times later. The results have been encouraging: attendance has improved, and students report feeling more alert. Critics point out, however, that later starting times create problems for working parents and for after-school activities, and they argue that the benefits may not justify the cost of reorganizing transportation and schedules.

questions.stem: The main purpose of the first paragraph is to -
options: present a common explanation that the passage will challenge
prove that teenagers spend too much time in front of screens
explain how parents should wake their children
argue that teachers are responsible for poor discipline
questions.explanation: הפסקה מציגה את ההסבר המקובל (משמעת, מסכים), ומסיימת ב-however: מחקרים חדשים מצביעים על הסבר ביולוגי. כלומר — היא מציגה עמדה שהקטע יערער עליה.

questions.stem: According to the second paragraph, many teenagers fall asleep late because -
options: they need less sleep than children do
their brains release melatonin later than in childhood
they usually go to bed too early
their internal clock stops working during adolescence
questions.explanation: בפסקה 2: המוח מפריש מלטונין כשעתיים מאוחר יותר מאשר בילדות, ולכן בני נוער לא מרגישים עייפים עד חצות. הם דווקא צריכים 8–10 שעות שינה, כך שאפשרות 1 שגויה. השעון "זז" (shifts) ולא מפסיק לפעול.

questions.stem: Which of the following is stated in the third paragraph about depression?
options: It is the main cause of lower grades among teenagers.
It is caused by early school starting times.
It is linked to lack of sleep, but it is not clear which causes which.
It affects mainly young drivers.
questions.explanation: "the direction of cause and effect is not yet clear" — יש קשר בין חוסר שינה לדיכאון, אך לא ידוע מה גורם למה. אפשרות 2 קובעת סיבתיות שהקטע נמנע ממנה במפורש.

questions.stem: Critics of later school starting times argue that -
options: students do not actually become more alert
attendance decreases when school starts later
teenagers will simply go to bed even later
the practical difficulties may outweigh the advantages
questions.explanation: המבקרים טוענים שהשינוי יוצר בעיות להורים עובדים ולפעילויות אחר הצהריים, ושהתועלת אולי אינה מצדיקה את העלות. אפשרויות 1–2 סותרות את התוצאות המעודדות שתוארו.

readingComprehension.title: The Printing Revolution
paragraphs: Before the middle of the fifteenth century, books in Europe were copied by hand, usually by monks working in monasteries. A single copy of the Bible could take more than a year to produce, and books were therefore rare and extremely expensive. Only the Church, universities, and the wealthiest families could afford to own them.

Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith from the German city of Mainz, developed a printing press that used movable metal type. Individual letters could be arranged to form a page, printed, and then rearranged for the next page. Gutenberg did not invent printing itself — craftsmen in China and Korea had used movable type centuries earlier — but his system was the first to be fast, durable, and well suited to alphabetic languages.

The new technology spread with remarkable speed. By 1500, printing presses were operating in more than two hundred European cities, and millions of books had been produced. As prices fell, reading was no longer limited to a small elite. Merchants, craftsmen, and eventually ordinary townspeople began to buy books, pamphlets, and calendars.

Historians continue to debate the long-term effects of printing. Some argue that it made the Protestant Reformation and the Scientific Revolution possible, since new ideas could now circulate widely before authorities were able to suppress them. Others warn against giving a single invention too much credit, noting that rising literacy and growing trade were already changing European society before Gutenberg's press appeared.

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, books were expensive before 1450 mainly because -
options: they were produced slowly by hand
only the Church was allowed to sell them
the monks charged high prices for their work
very few people knew how to read
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1: העתקה ידנית של ספר אחד יכלה לארוך יותר משנה, ולכן (therefore) הספרים היו נדירים ויקרים. אפשרות 4 אולי נכונה היסטורית, אך אינה מוזכרת בקטע.

questions.stem: What does the second paragraph say about Gutenberg's achievement?
options: He was the first person in history to print with movable type.
He improved a technique that already existed, making it more practical.
He learned how to print from craftsmen in China and Korea.
He developed a printing method that suited only the German language.
questions.explanation: "Gutenberg did not invent printing itself" — דפוס באותיות נעות היה קיים בסין ובקוריאה. החידוש שלו: שיטה מהירה, עמידה ומתאימה לשפות אלפביתיות. אין טענה שלמד מהם (אפשרות 3).

questions.stem: The word "elite" in the third paragraph refers to -
options: merchants and craftsmen
ordinary townspeople
printers working in European cities
a small, privileged group of people
questions.explanation: המשפט אומר שהקריאה כבר לא הוגבלה ל-small elite — קבוצה קטנה ומיוחסת (הכנסייה, האוניברסיטאות והעשירים מפסקה 1). סוחרים ובעלי מלאכה הם דווקא אלה שהצטרפו לקוראים אחר כך.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the view of the "others" mentioned in the last paragraph?
options: Printing had no effect at all on European society.
The Reformation led to the invention of printing.
The importance of printing should not be exaggerated.
Authorities managed to suppress most new ideas.
questions.explanation: "warn against giving a single invention too much credit" — הם מזהירים מלייחס לדפוס יותר מדי חשיבות, כי שינויים אחרים כבר היו בעיצומם. הם אינם טוענים שלא הייתה לו השפעה כלל (אפשרות 1 קיצונית מדי).

readingComprehension.title: Microplastics in the Ocean
paragraphs: Every year, millions of tons of plastic waste enter the world's oceans. While floating bottles and bags are easy to see, scientists are increasingly concerned about something far less visible: microplastics, pieces of plastic smaller than five millimeters. Some are manufactured at this size, such as the tiny beads once common in cosmetics, but most result from larger items slowly breaking apart under the effect of sunlight and waves.

Because they are so small, microplastics are easily swallowed by marine animals, from tiny plankton to whales. Laboratory studies have shown that they can damage the digestive systems of fish and reduce their ability to reproduce. In addition, microplastics tend to absorb toxic chemicals from the surrounding water, which may then be passed up the food chain.

Humans are not protected from this problem. Microplastics have been found in seafood, table salt, and even drinking water. The effects on human health remain uncertain, however. So far, there is little direct evidence that the amounts people typically consume cause harm, and researchers stress that more long-term studies are needed before firm conclusions can be drawn.

Removing microplastics from the ocean is practically impossible, so most experts agree that the only realistic solution is to stop them from entering it in the first place. Several countries have already banned plastic microbeads, and some are considering stricter rules on single-use plastics. Others, however, believe that improved recycling and waste management, rather than bans, will prove more effective in the long run.

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, most microplastics -
options: are manufactured for use in cosmetics
are larger than five millimeters
are formed when larger pieces of plastic break apart
float on the surface of the water where they can be seen
questions.explanation: "most result from larger items slowly breaking apart" — רוב המיקרופלסטיק נוצר מפירוק של פריטים גדולים. רק חלק (Some) מיוצר בגודל זה, כמו החרוזים בקוסמטיקה.

questions.stem: The second paragraph mentions all of the following as possible dangers of microplastics EXCEPT -
options: damage to the digestive systems of fish
a reduced ability of fish to reproduce
toxic chemicals passed up the food chain
the death of large numbers of whales
questions.explanation: לווייתנים מוזכרים רק כדוגמה לבעלי חיים שבולעים מיקרופלסטיק, ולא נאמר שהם מתים בגללו. שלוש הסכנות האחרות מופיעות במפורש בפסקה.

questions.stem: What is the main point of the third paragraph?
options: Microplastics in drinking water are a proven health hazard.
Although people consume microplastics, the effect on their health is still unknown.
People should avoid seafood because it contains microplastics.
Long-term studies have shown that microplastics are harmless to humans.
questions.explanation: הפסקה אומרת שמיקרופלסטיק נמצא במזון ובמים, אך ההשפעה על בריאות האדם עדיין אינה ודאית (uncertain) ונדרשים מחקרים ארוכי טווח. אפשרויות 1 ו-4 קובעות מסקנות שהקטע נמנע מהן.

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that -
options: there is disagreement about the best way to keep microplastics out of the ocean
effective methods of removing microplastics from the water have been developed
recycling has already solved the problem of microplastics
all countries have agreed to ban single-use plastics
questions.explanation: חלק מהמדינות בוחרות באיסורים, ואחרים (Others, however) מאמינים שמחזור וניהול פסולת יעילים יותר — כלומר יש מחלוקת על הדרך. הסרה מהים מתוארת כבלתי אפשרית כמעט, ולכן אפשרות 2 שגויה.

readingComprehension.title: The Future of the Office
paragraphs: Before 2020, working from home was a privilege enjoyed by a relatively small number of employees. The COVID-19 pandemic changed that almost overnight. Within weeks, millions of office workers around the world were holding meetings by video and sharing documents online. What began as an emergency measure soon became, for many companies, a permanent way of working.

Supporters of remote work point to several advantages. Employees save the time and money they once spent commuting, and many report a better balance between work and family life. Companies, for their part, can reduce the cost of office space and hire talented people who live far from their headquarters. Some studies have even found that productivity rose when employees worked from home.

Yet the picture is not entirely positive. Other studies suggest that productivity gains are concentrated in routine, individual tasks, while work that depends on creativity and cooperation suffers. Younger employees in particular may miss out on the informal learning that comes from watching experienced colleagues. Many remote workers also report feelings of isolation and find it hard to separate their working hours from their free time.

As a result, a growing number of organizations have adopted a "hybrid" model, in which employees spend some days in the office and others at home. Whether this compromise will capture the benefits of both arrangements, or simply combine their disadvantages, is a question that researchers and managers are only beginning to answer.

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, the COVID-19 pandemic -
options: led many companies to adopt remote work very quickly
made working from home a privilege for a few employees
put an end to the use of video meetings
forced most companies to close their offices permanently
questions.explanation: "changed that almost overnight" ו-"Within weeks" — המגפה הובילה למעבר מהיר לעבודה מרחוק. לפני 2020 זו הייתה פריבילגיה (אפשרות 2 מתארת את המצב הקודם). הקטע לא אומר שמשרדים נסגרו לצמיתות.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the second paragraph as an advantage of remote work?
options: saving time on travel to work
lower spending on office space
access to talented people who live far away
higher salaries for employees
questions.explanation: הפסקה מזכירה חיסכון בזמן נסיעה (commuting), הוזלת שטחי משרד וגיוס עובדים מרוחקים. משכורות גבוהות יותר אינן מוזכרות.

questions.stem: According to the third paragraph, younger employees may be harmed by remote work because they -
options: are less productive at routine tasks
have fewer chances to learn from experienced colleagues
prefer to work in the office with their friends
find it difficult to use video technology
questions.explanation: "miss out on the informal learning that comes from watching experienced colleagues" — עובדים צעירים מפסידים למידה לא פורמלית מעמיתים מנוסים. דווקא במשימות שגרתיות נמצאה עלייה בפריון.

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the hybrid model can best be described as -
options: enthusiastic
strongly critical
uncertain
indifferent
questions.explanation: המחבר מציג שתי אפשרויות — המודל ישלב את היתרונות או את החסרונות — ואומר שהתשובה רק מתחילה להתברר. זו עמדה של חוסר ודאות, לא התלהבות ולא ביקורת.

readingComprehension.title: How Habits Form
paragraphs: Every day, people perform hundreds of actions without thinking about them: brushing their teeth, locking the door, checking their phones. Psychologists estimate that a large share of our daily behavior is not the result of conscious decisions but of habits, automatic responses triggered by familiar situations.

Researchers often describe a habit as a loop with three parts. First comes a cue, such as a time of day, a place, or a feeling. The cue triggers a routine, the behavior itself. Finally, there is a reward, a pleasant result that makes the brain more likely to repeat the routine the next time the cue appears. Over time, the link between cue and routine becomes so strong that the behavior occurs almost by itself.

This explains why bad habits are so difficult to break. Simply deciding to stop rarely works, because the cue is still present and the brain still expects the reward. Many experts therefore recommend keeping the cue and the reward but replacing the routine. A person who snacks when bored in the afternoon, for example, might take a short walk instead, which also provides a break and a sense of relief.

How long does it take to form a new habit? A popular belief holds that twenty-one days are enough. However, a study conducted at University College London found that the time varied enormously between participants, from a few weeks to most of a year, with an average of about two months. The researchers also found that missing a single day did not seriously harm the process.

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, habits are -
options: decisions that people make with great care
automatic reactions to familiar situations
actions that people perform only rarely
the result of conscious planning
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1 הרגלים מוגדרים כ-automatic responses triggered by familiar situations — תגובות אוטומטיות למצבים מוכרים, ולא החלטות מודעות.

questions.stem: In the habit loop described in paragraph 2, the reward -
options: appears before the cue
replaces the routine
makes it more likely that the routine will be repeated
is always a feeling of boredom
questions.explanation: בפסקה 2 נכתב שהתגמול makes the brain more likely to repeat the routine — מגביר את הסיכוי שהשגרה תחזור.

questions.stem: The example of the afternoon walk (paragraph 3) is given in order to -
options: show that exercise is more important than eating
explain why people feel bored in the afternoon
prove that bad habits cannot be changed
illustrate how a routine can be replaced while the cue and reward stay the same
questions.explanation: ההליכה היא דוגמה להמלצה שלפניה: להשאיר את הרמז ואת התגמול ולהחליף רק את השגרה. שאלות ׳for what purpose׳ בודקות את תפקיד הדוגמה בטיעון.

questions.stem: What does the London study (paragraph 4) suggest about the popular belief mentioned in the same paragraph?
options: It is too simple, since the time needed varies greatly from person to person.
It is accurate for most people.
It underestimates the harm of missing a single day.
It applies only to bad habits.
questions.explanation: המחקר מצא טווח רחב — משבועות ספורים ועד כמעט שנה — ולכן האמונה ש-21 יום מספיקים היא פשטנית. המחקר דווקא מצא שדילוג על יום אחד לא פוגע משמעותית.

readingComprehension.title: Drinking Water from the Sea
paragraphs: Although about seventy percent of the Earth's surface is covered by water, only a tiny fraction of it is fresh water that people can drink. As populations grow and droughts become more frequent, many countries have turned to desalination, the process of removing salt from seawater.

The most common method today is reverse osmosis. Seawater is pushed at high pressure through special membranes with extremely small holes. Water molecules pass through, while salt and most other substances are left behind. Compared with older methods, which boiled the water and collected the steam, reverse osmosis uses far less energy.

Israel is often cited as a success story. Since the early 2000s, the country has built several large desalination plants along its Mediterranean coast, and today a large share of its household water comes from the sea. As a result, a country that once suffered from chronic water shortages now has a relatively stable supply, even in dry years.

Desalination is not without problems, however. The plants still require a great deal of electricity, which is often produced by burning fossil fuels. In addition, the process produces brine, a very salty liquid that is returned to the sea and may harm marine life near the outlet pipes. Engineers are therefore searching for ways to power plants with renewable energy and to dispose of brine more safely.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, countries have turned to desalination mainly because -
options: most of the Earth's water is already fresh
fresh water is limited while demand is increasing
seawater is cleaner than river water
desalination is cheaper than any other source of water
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1: רק חלק זעיר מהמים ראויים לשתייה, והאוכלוסייה גדלה ובצורות מתרבות — כלומר מחסור מול ביקוש גובר.

questions.stem: In reverse osmosis, the membranes -
options: boil the water and collect the steam
add salt to the water
allow water molecules through but block salt
require no pressure at all
questions.explanation: בפסקה 2: Water molecules pass through, while salt... are left behind. הרתחה ואיסוף אדים הם השיטה הישנה.

questions.stem: The word "chronic" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to -
options: sudden
minor
imaginary
long-lasting
questions.explanation: chronic = כרוני, מתמשך. המדינה סבלה ממחסור במים לאורך זמן, בניגוד לאספקה היציבה של היום.

questions.stem: The main purpose of the last paragraph is to -
options: present some drawbacks of desalination and possible solutions
argue that desalination should be stopped
explain how brine is produced from fresh water
compare Israel with other countries
questions.explanation: הפסקה נפתחת ב-not without problems, however, מציגה בעיות (חשמל, תמלחת) ומסיימת בפתרונות שמהנדסים מחפשים. היא אינה קוראת להפסיק את ההתפלה.

readingComprehension.title: The Power of the Placebo
paragraphs: A placebo is a treatment with no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill or an injection of salt water. Yet patients who receive placebos often report real improvements in their symptoms. This puzzling phenomenon, known as the placebo effect, has fascinated doctors for centuries.

The placebo effect is especially strong for conditions that are influenced by the brain's own processing, such as pain, nausea, and anxiety. Brain-imaging studies have shown that when patients expect a treatment to reduce their pain, their brains may release natural painkillers. In other words, expectation alone can produce measurable physical changes.

Because of this effect, new drugs are usually tested in controlled trials. One group of patients receives the real drug, while another receives a placebo, and neither the patients nor the doctors know who received which. A drug is considered effective only if it performs significantly better than the placebo. Without such comparisons, researchers might mistake the placebo effect for the action of the drug.

Perhaps the most surprising finding is that placebos can work even when patients know they are taking them. In several small studies, patients with chronic conditions who were openly given "honest placebos" still reported feeling better. Researchers caution that placebos cannot shrink tumors or cure infections, but they suggest that the ritual of receiving care may itself have healing power.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, the placebo effect is strongest for -
options: infections caused by bacteria
conditions such as pain and anxiety
diseases that require surgery
patients who do not expect any improvement
questions.explanation: בפסקה 2: especially strong for conditions... such as pain, nausea, and anxiety.

questions.stem: The brain-imaging studies mentioned in paragraph 2 show that -
options: placebos contain hidden painkillers
expectation can cause real changes in the body
patients only imagine that they feel better
sugar pills are more effective than real drugs
questions.explanation: המחקרים הראו שציפייה גורמת למוח לשחרר משככי כאבים טבעיים — expectation alone can produce measurable physical changes. התשובה השלישית הפוכה: השינוי אמיתי ולא דמיוני.

questions.stem: In a controlled trial (paragraph 3), a new drug is considered effective if -
options: patients in both groups improve equally
the doctors know which patients received the drug
it works clearly better than the placebo
it is given to patients openly
questions.explanation: בפסקה 3: considered effective only if it performs significantly better than the placebo.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements would the researchers in paragraph 4 most likely agree with?
options: Placebos can replace all medical treatment.
Honest placebos have no effect at all.
Placebos are useful for curing infections.
Placebos have limits, but the experience of being cared for may help patients.
questions.explanation: החוקרים מזהירים שפלצבו לא מכווץ גידולים ולא מרפא זיהומים, אך מציעים שטקס קבלת הטיפול עצמו מרפא. לכן יש לו מגבלות, אך גם תועלת.

readingComprehension.title: The Library of Alexandria
paragraphs: In the third century BCE, the rulers of Egypt set out to build the greatest collection of knowledge in the ancient world. The Library of Alexandria was part of a larger research institution where scholars from across the Mediterranean studied mathematics, astronomy, medicine, and literature.

The library's leaders were determined to acquire every book they could find. According to one story, ships that entered the harbor of Alexandria were searched, and any scrolls on board were taken to be copied. The library kept the originals and returned the copies to their owners. Whether or not this story is true, it reflects the library's enormous ambition.

The library is famous today largely because of its destruction, which is often imagined as a single dramatic fire. In reality, historians believe that its decline was slow. Funding was reduced, scholars were driven out during periods of political unrest, and parts of the city were damaged in a series of wars over several centuries. By the time the last remains disappeared, the library had long since lost its importance.

The popular image of a single catastrophe may persist because it offers a simple lesson about the fragility of knowledge. The more complex reality, however, carries a lesson of its own: great institutions are rarely destroyed overnight. More often, they fade away when societies stop supporting them.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, the Library of Alexandria was -
options: a small private collection of literature
part of a larger center of learning
built mainly to store government records
open only to Egyptian scholars
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1: part of a larger research institution where scholars from across the Mediterranean studied — חלק ממוסד מחקר גדול, ולא רק למלומדים מצרים.

questions.stem: The story about the ships (paragraph 2) is mentioned in order to -
options: prove that the library stole books
describe the history of the harbor
show how eager the library was to collect books
explain why the library was destroyed
questions.explanation: הכותב מסייג (Whether or not this story is true) ומסביר שהסיפור reflects the library's enormous ambition — הוא ממחיש את השאיפה לאסוף ספרים, ולא מוכיח דבר.

questions.stem: According to historians, the library -
options: was destroyed in one great fire
was never actually built
was moved to another city
declined gradually over a long period
questions.explanation: בפסקה 3: historians believe that its decline was slow — דעיכה הדרגתית לאורך מאות שנים, בניגוד לדימוי של שריפה אחת.

questions.stem: What lesson does the author draw in the last paragraph?
options: Institutions usually disappear slowly when they lose society's support.
Libraries should be built far from cities.
Fires are the main danger to knowledge.
Ancient scholars were not interested in politics.
questions.explanation: המשפט האחרון: they fade away when societies stop supporting them — מוסדות נעלמים בהדרגה כשהחברה מפסיקה לתמוך בהם.

readingComprehension.title: When Languages Disappear
paragraphs: Linguists estimate that there are about seven thousand languages spoken in the world today. Yet this diversity is unevenly distributed: a handful of major languages are spoken by most of the world's population, while thousands of others have only a few thousand speakers, or even fewer. Many experts predict that a large proportion of these smaller languages could disappear by the end of this century.

A language rarely dies because its speakers suddenly stop using it. More often, the process takes several generations. Parents who speak a minority language may decide that their children will have better opportunities if they speak the dominant language of the country. The children grow up understanding their parents' language but speaking it less and less, and their own children may not learn it at all.

The loss of a language involves more than the loss of words. Each language contains knowledge accumulated over centuries, such as names for local plants and their medical uses, ways of describing the landscape, and stories that preserve a community's history. When the last speakers die, much of this knowledge may vanish with them.

Some communities have managed to reverse the trend. Hebrew, which for centuries was used mainly in prayer and writing, became the everyday language of millions of people. More recently, communities in New Zealand and Wales have set up schools in which children are taught entirely in the local language. Such efforts show that decline is not inevitable, but they require strong commitment from both communities and governments.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, the world's languages -
options: are spoken by roughly equal numbers of people
are increasing in number every year
are very unevenly distributed among speakers
will all disappear by the end of the century
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1: this diversity is unevenly distributed — מעט שפות מדוברות על ידי רוב האנשים. התשובה האחרונה מוגזמת (all).

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, a language usually disappears -
options: gradually, as each generation uses it less
immediately after a war
because speakers forget it in old age
when governments ban it
questions.explanation: בפסקה 2: the process takes several generations — כל דור משתמש בשפה פחות, עד שהנכדים כבר לא לומדים אותה.

questions.stem: The examples in paragraph 3 (names of plants, stories) are given to show that -
options: minority languages have small vocabularies
plants have different names in every country
stories are more important than words
a language carries a community's knowledge and history
questions.explanation: הדוגמאות ממחישות את טענת הפתיחה של הפסקה: The loss of a language involves more than the loss of words — שפה נושאת ידע והיסטוריה.

questions.stem: The case of Hebrew is mentioned in paragraph 4 as an example of -
options: a language that disappeared
a language that was revived for daily use
a language used only in schools
a language spoken mainly in Wales
questions.explanation: עברית שימשה בעיקר לתפילה ולכתיבה והפכה לשפת היומיום של מיליונים — דוגמה להיפוך המגמה (reverse the trend).

readingComprehension.title: Can Machines Be Creative?
paragraphs: Computer programs can now write poems, compose music, and produce paintings in the style of famous artists. Some of these works are so convincing that audiences cannot tell whether they were made by a person or a machine. This development has revived an old question: can a machine be truly creative?

Supporters of the idea argue that creativity is simply the ability to produce something that is both new and valuable. By this definition, they say, the source of the work does not matter. If a program composes a melody that listeners find beautiful and that no one has heard before, it has done what we expect of a creative person.

Critics disagree. They point out that such programs learn by analyzing enormous numbers of existing works and then producing new combinations of the patterns they have found. In their view, this is closer to skilled imitation than to genuine invention. A human artist, they argue, creates out of experiences, emotions, and intentions, none of which a program possesses.

Many artists, however, see the debate as less important than the practical question of how to use these tools. Some use programs to suggest ideas, which they then develop and change. For them, the machine is neither a rival nor a genius but an instrument, much like the camera, which was once feared as the end of painting and instead became an art form of its own.

questions.stem: According to the supporters described in paragraph 2, -
options: only humans can produce valuable work
the source of a work is irrelevant if the work is new and valuable
music is the only creative art
audiences should always know who made a work
questions.explanation: התומכים מגדירים יצירתיות כיצירת דבר חדש ובעל ערך, ולכן the source of the work does not matter.

questions.stem: The critics in paragraph 3 believe that computer programs -
options: are more creative than most human artists
have their own emotions and intentions
mainly recombine patterns from existing works
cannot produce anything that sounds new
questions.explanation: לדברי המבקרים, התוכנות מנתחות יצירות קיימות ומייצרות צירופים חדשים של דפוסים — closer to skilled imitation. הם לא טוענים שהתוצאה לא נשמעת חדשה.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the camera in the last paragraph?
options: To argue that photography is not a real art
To show that new technologies always destroy older arts
To explain how computer programs take pictures
To suggest that a feared new tool may become a means of artistic expression
questions.explanation: המצלמה עוררה חשש שתביא לקץ הציור, ובמקום זאת הפכה לאמנות בפני עצמה. ההשוואה מרמזת שגם תוכנות עשויות להפוך לכלי אמנותי.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the structure of the passage?
options: A question is raised, two opposing views are presented, and a practical perspective is added.
A problem is described and a single solution is proposed.
The history of computers is told in chronological order.
An experiment is described and its results are analyzed.
questions.explanation: פסקה 1 מעלה שאלה, פסקאות 2–3 מציגות עמדות מנוגדות (תומכים ומבקרים), ופסקה 4 מוסיפה נקודת מבט מעשית של אמנים.

readingComprehension.title: In Praise of Boredom
paragraphs: Boredom has a bad reputation. It is usually seen as an unpleasant state to be escaped as quickly as possible, and modern technology makes escape easier than ever: at the first sign of boredom, most people reach for their phones. Yet a growing number of psychologists argue that boredom may actually be good for us.

In one well-known experiment, participants were first asked to perform a deliberately dull task, copying numbers from a telephone directory, for fifteen minutes. They were then asked to think of as many uses as possible for a pair of plastic cups. Compared with a group that had not done the dull task, the bored participants came up with more ideas, and their ideas were more original.

Researchers suggest that when the outside world offers little stimulation, the mind begins to wander. This daydreaming allows the brain to make unexpected connections between ideas, which is an important part of creative thinking. Boredom may also act as a signal, telling us that our current activity is not satisfying and pushing us to look for more meaningful goals.

None of this means that boredom is always beneficial. Chronic boredom has been linked to poor concentration and unhealthy habits. The point, researchers say, is that brief periods of boredom are not necessarily a problem to be solved. Allowing ourselves to be bored occasionally, instead of filling every free moment, might make us both more creative and more aware of what we really want.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, modern technology -
options: makes people more bored than in the past
makes it easy to avoid feeling bored
has improved boredom's reputation
is recommended by psychologists
questions.explanation: בפסקה 1: modern technology makes escape easier than ever — קל לברוח מהשעמום (למשל לטלפון).

questions.stem: In the experiment described in paragraph 2, the participants who had done the dull task -
options: refused to complete the second task
produced fewer ideas than the other group
produced more and more original ideas
copied the ideas of the other group
questions.explanation: המשתתפים המשועממים came up with more ideas, and their ideas were more original — יותר רעיונות ומקוריים יותר.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, boredom may help creativity because it -
options: encourages the mind to wander and connect ideas
improves people's memory for numbers
makes people work faster
reduces the need for sleep
questions.explanation: בפסקה 3: כשהסביבה לא מגרה, the mind begins to wander, וחלימה בהקיץ מאפשרת חיבורים לא צפויים בין רעיונות.

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward boredom can best be described as -
options: completely negative
enthusiastic without any reservations
indifferent
generally positive, with some reservations
questions.explanation: הכותב מציג יתרונות לשעמום, אך מסייג בפסקה 4: None of this means that boredom is always beneficial. לכן העמדה חיובית בעיקרה, עם הסתייגויות.

readingComprehension.title: The Long Journey of the Monarch Butterfly
paragraphs: Each autumn, millions of monarch butterflies leave Canada and the northern United States and fly south to the mountains of central Mexico, a journey of up to 4,000 kilometers. For an insect that weighs less than a gram, it is one of the most remarkable migrations in the animal kingdom.

What makes the journey even more mysterious is that no single butterfly completes the full round trip. The monarchs that fly south in autumn spend the winter in Mexico and begin the return journey in spring, but they die along the way. Their offspring continue north, and it takes three or four generations to reach Canada again. The butterflies that fly south the following autumn have therefore never made the trip before.

How do they find their way? Scientists have discovered that monarchs use the position of the sun as a compass, correcting for its movement across the sky with an internal clock located in their antennae. There is also evidence that they can sense the Earth's magnetic field, which may help them on cloudy days.

In recent decades, the number of monarchs reaching Mexico has dropped sharply. Researchers point to several causes, including the loss of milkweed, the only plant on which monarch caterpillars can feed, as well as the destruction of forests in their winter habitat and changes in climate. Conservation programs now encourage people across North America to plant milkweed in their gardens.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, the butterflies that fly south in autumn -
options: have made the journey several times before
have never made the journey before
spend the summer in Mexico
complete the whole round trip
questions.explanation: המשפט האחרון בפסקה 2: The butterflies that fly south the following autumn have therefore never made the trip before.

questions.stem: The word "offspring" in paragraph 2 refers to the butterflies' -
options: enemies
parents
young
food
questions.explanation: offspring = צאצאים. הפרפרים מתים בדרך, וצאצאיהם ממשיכים צפונה.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, the internal clock in the monarchs' antennae helps them -
options: sense the Earth's magnetic field
find milkweed plants
know when to lay eggs
adjust for the changing position of the sun
questions.explanation: בפסקה 3: correcting for its movement across the sky with an internal clock located in their antennae — השעון מתקן את תנועת השמש. השדה המגנטי הוא מנגנון נפרד.

questions.stem: Why do conservation programs encourage people to plant milkweed?
options: Because monarch caterpillars cannot feed on any other plant
Because milkweed protects forests in Mexico
Because milkweed changes the climate
Because adult butterflies use it to find their way
questions.explanation: בפסקה 4: milkweed הוא the only plant on which monarch caterpillars can feed, והיעלמותו היא אחת הסיבות לירידה במספר הפרפרים.
